package.name: typesafe
package.packageFile:
# TYPESAFE, fully declarative.
#
# One vendor endpoint, POST /v1/systemone, answers typed questions about a piece of state:
# pick an option, place on a scale, or say whether a statement holds. The answer is a value
# and a probability distribution, never prose, so a workflow branches on it directly.
#
# Four nodes over the one call: three ask a single question of one type, and the fourth
# sends a whole map of questions in one round trip, which is how the vendor is meant to be
# used when several judgements share the same state.

name: typesafe
displayName: TypeSafe
description: Typed decisions from Jev, TypeSafe's System One model; a value and a probability, never prose
version: 1.0.0
category: ai
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1789700088/gravity/icons/typesafe_ai_logo.jpg

features:
  - Choose one option from a described list, with a probability for each
  - Score state on an ordered scale of described levels
  - Answer whether a statement is true, as a probability
  - Ask several questions of one state in a single call

allowedHosts:
  - api.typesafe.ai

requires:
  executorVersion: ">=1.6.0"
  credential: [bearer]
  transport: [json]

credentials.typesafeCredential.yaml:
name: typesafeCredential
displayName: TypeSafe
description: Credentials for the TypeSafe API
documentationUrl: https://console.typesafe.ai/settings/keys

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your TypeSafe API key
    placeholder: ts-

files.api/events.yaml:
# One row per output connector, in interface.yaml order.

- emit: answers
  from: response
  value: "return response.answers"

- emit: usage
  from: response
  value: >-
    return {
      model: response.model,
      inputTokens: (response.usage || {}).input_tokens || 0,
      outputTokens: (response.usage || {}).output_tokens || 0
    }
files.api/run.yaml:
# One synchronous call carrying the whole question map as given. The vendor evaluates every
# question in parallel and in isolation against the one state, which is the point of
# sending them together.
#
# STATE MAY BE STRUCTURE. The field is a string so it can be typed or templated, but the
# vendor reads a JSON object or array as named fields rather than as prose, so a value that
# is a whole JSON document is parsed before it is sent. Prose stays prose.

- name: ask
  method: POST
  url: https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone
  credential:
    scheme: bearer
    token: "{{ credentials.typesafeCredential.apiKey }}"
  headers:
    Content-Type: application/json
  transport: json
  timeoutMs: 60000
  # 529 is the vendor's own overloaded code, alongside the usual rate limit and server errors.
  retry:
    attempts: 3
    backoff: exponential
    on: [429, 500, 502, 503, 504, 529]

  body:
    model: "return config.model || 'jev-latest'"
    state: >-
      return (typeof config.state === 'string'
        && ((config.state.trim().startsWith('{') && config.state.trim().endsWith('}'))
          || (config.state.trim().startsWith('[') && config.state.trim().endsWith(']'))))
        ? JSON.parse(config.state)
        : config.state
    questions: "return config.questions"

  error:
    # An empty answer map is a failure whatever the status was.
    when: "return !Object.keys(response.answers || {}).length"
    message: >-
      return 'TypeSafe returned no answers.'
        + (response.error ? ' ' + JSON.stringify(response.error) : '')
        + (response.detail ? ' ' + JSON.stringify(response.detail) : '')
files.config.yaml:
configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [state, questions]
  properties:
    state:
      type: string
      title: State
      description: >-
        What to judge: a message, a passage, a record. Text is sent as text; a JSON object or
        array (for example {{ toJSON signal.x }}) is sent as structure, which the model reads
        better than prose when the data has named fields.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
      "ui:ai":
        editable: true
    questions:
      type: object
      title: Questions
      description: >-
        Question key to question, as JSON. Each has a type of choice, score or noul,
        instructions, and criteria: an option map for a choice, an ordered list of levels
        for a score, and an optional true and false description for a noul.
      default: {}
      "ui:field": template
      "ui:ai":
        editable: true
    model:
      type: string
      title: Model
      description: jev-latest is the stable release; jev-preview is the newest build.
      enum: [jev-latest, jev-preview]
      default: jev-latest
"ui:order": [state, questions, model]
files.interface.yaml:
inputs:
  - name: signal
    type: object
    description: Data from previous nodes
    required: false

outputs:
  - name: answers
    type: object
    description: Each question's answer, by key
  - name: usage
    type: object
    description: model, inputTokens, outputTokens

credentials:
  - name: typesafeCredential
    required: true
    displayName: TypeSafe
files.node.yaml:
type: TypeSafeQuestions
# One call, one reply: the endpoint answers synchronously however many questions it carries.
kind: PromiseNode

name: TypeSafe Questions
category: AI
color: "#1D4ED8"
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1789700088/gravity/icons/typesafe_ai_logo.jpg

description: Ask several typed questions of one state in a single call; every answer comes back keyed

whenToUse: >-
  Make several judgements about the same text or data at once and get them all back in one
  round trip: route a message and rate its urgency and flag whether it needs a refund,
  each as its own typed answer under its own key. Questions are a JSON map in the vendor's
  own shape, mixing choice, score and noul freely, so it suits an Agent or an upstream
  step that composes questions from data, and any case where one question per node would
  mean sending the same state many times. For a single question of one kind a dedicated
  node gives the answer as flat fields.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (who-can-run-it.md). Compulsory on every node, so that a node nobody
# thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # A pure read: the same state and questions give the same answers, and nothing is
  # written anywhere.
  cacheable: true
files.test.yaml:
# Asserts the SHAPE, not the verdicts: one answer per question, each of the type asked for.
# The state is structure here, to prove the JSON path reaches the vendor as an object.

testData:
  config:
    state: '{"message": "My card was charged twice for order A-104 and I want the second charge refunded.", "order_id": "A-104"}'
    questions:
      team:
        type: choice
        instructions: Which team should handle this message?
        criteria:
          billing: Charges, refunds, invoices and payment methods
          shipping: Where an order is, delivery dates, damaged parcels
      urgency:
        type: score
        instructions: How urgent is this message?
        criteria:
          - Can wait a week
          - Should be handled today
          - Needs a reply within the hour
      refund:
        type: noul
        instructions: Is the customer asking for a refund?
    model: jev-latest
  inputs:
    signal: {}
  expect:
    answers: >-
      return ['billing', 'shipping'].includes(output.answers.team.choice)
        && output.answers.urgency.score >= 0 && output.answers.urgency.score <= 2
        && output.answers.refund.noul >= 0 && output.answers.refund.noul <= 1
    usage: "return output.usage.inputTokens > 0 && typeof output.usage.model === 'string'"
